subject: Production: client-side timeouts from streaming silence window (urgent)
messages:
From: Dave Liu <dave.liu@novamed.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: support@novamed.ai
Date: 2028-03-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: sudden increase in streaming disconnects — clients timing out

Sergio —

We're seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx/429 responses on our streaming chat connections since ~07:45 PT. Clients report a ~20–40s silent window where the stream produces no tokens and then the client-side SDK times out and retries aggressively. That retry behavior is triggering a secondary wave of 429s and what looks like a retry amplification pattern.

Quick snapshot from our side: 5xx rate spiked from 0.2% -> 3.8% across the last 30m; median streaming response gap ~32s for affected sessions. We attached session traces for three request IDs (rids: 7f8a2c, 7f8a2d, 7f8a30).

Can you confirm whether there were any deploys, config changes, or routing anomalies on Redwood's side? This is impacting our clinical triage UX — we need an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Dave Liu
CTO, NovaMed

Attachment: novamed-session-traces-20280310.txt (3 session traces, 2KB)

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Dave Liu <dave.liu@novamed.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-10T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden increase in streaming disconnects — clients timing out

Dave — thanks for the heads up and for sending traces. I'm escalating immediately. Initial read: this looks like a short 'quiet window' where the server-side stream pauses (no tokens emitted) and the client-side SDK times out and retries; the retries are producing a secondary quota/429 amplification.

Immediate plan (next 60m):
- Can you share one full request header for rid 7f8a2c (we need model id and sequence length)?
- We'll enable extended keepalive/heartbeat probes for your tenant and bump server-side idle timeout to 45s to reduce premature disconnects.
- We'll temporarily route your traffic to a dedicated pool (if capacity permits) to remove noisy multi-tenant interference.
- Ask clients to back off retries to exponential with jitter (we'll send recommended config snippet).

I've looped in Marissa (infra SRE) and Vanessa (CS lead) to own the infra mitigation and customer comms resp. We'll follow up with a short mutual action plan and timeline.

— Sergio
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Phone: +1-415-555-0199

[Incident ticket created: INC-2094]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: NovaMed production — quiet-window + retry amplification — need infra & exec brief

Team —

NovaMed is seeing streaming silence windows (~30s) followed by client-side timeouts and aggressive retries; customer traces attached. External-facing impact: increased 5xxs and 429s, noticeable UX outage for clinical customers. Customer is on a high-value pilot (DEAL-7832). Execs want an ETA and rollback/mitigation plan.

Proposed immediate tasks (please ack ownership):
1) Marissa: open a P1 infra incident (INC-2094). Actionables: deploy a server-side idle-timeout bump to 45s for the NovaMed tenant, enable continuous keepalive probes, and route traffic to a dedicated pool if sustained errors persist. Collect kernel/gpu/serving-runtime logs for the 07:30–09:00 window. Attach: redwood-ln-kv-snapshot-20280310.json.
2) Vanessa: draft an external-facing status note for NovaMed (30–45 min ETA). Include mitigations and recommended SDK backoff config.
3) Evelyn: prep a two-paragraph exec note for the CRO/Head of Product with impact, revenue risk, and suggested next steps (canary plan to dedicated capacity + follow-up RCA).

Hypothesis thread: either (A) transient KV cache miss / kernel scheduling jitter causing token emission gaps, or (B) client SDK timeout misconfiguration that exposes normal gc/jit pauses as full disconnects. We need both infra traces and the client's client-side settings to narrow this down.

Please reply-all with immediate ownership and note any blockers (quota for dedicated pool, or change freeze windows).

— Sergio

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: NovaMed production — quiet-window + retry amplification — need infra & exec brief

Ack — opening INC-2094 now. Early findings: one worker in the serving pool reported a GC spike and a 28s execution stall at 07:46 PT; kernel scheduler logs show a short contention window on the instance serving Novamed traffic.

Actions taken (09:00–09:15):
- Pushed temporary config: idle-timeout -> 45s for NovaMed routes; enabled keepalive at 15s.
- Initiated routing rule to migrate ~30% of NovaMed traffic to dedicated pool (warm start) — pending quota increase approval; if accepted we'll migrate fully within 30m.
- Collected full runtime traces and uploaded to INC-2094 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2094). Attached local kv snapshot: redwood-ln-kv-snapshot-20280310.json.

Customer comms: Vanessa, draft outgoing note and I'll supply a short technical blurb for the root-cause timeline.

I'll provide a status update in 45m and escalate to execs if error rates don't drop below 0.5% by then.

— Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
